I'll write this for the benefit of all of the goats here:

Don't forget to go by the local church and ask around as to who is coordinating stuff in the local area. They have volunteer helpers who can come by and mow the lawn and stuff - often help with food and other short term necessities. They can be amazing when it comes to stuff like this - lots of experience - stuff you may not have thought of yet. Good people who really want to help, doesn't matter if you are a church type yourself. For them the reward is in the giving.

By God, the church bought my crippled uncle a proper fitting wheelchair - and later arranged for Jimmy Carter to come by and build him a wheelchair accessible home free of charge, (Habitat for Humanity.... they love giving you houses:) He also got himself a new wife there while he was at it:) Now they sell stuff together. They're doing better than a lot of us.

You get back on your feet, you give a little back. Charity. There is no shame in asking when the need is real.

Also - talk to the local United Way - they can get you hooked up with almost everything you'll be needing. They know everybody who matters when it comes to this... it is what they do full time.

Now here's a pro tip as I used to work in this field - most regions have these private charitable type "help" agencies that are staffed with counselors. If your needs are going to be longer term it really pays to hook up with one of these people. The United Way will know who they are. The reason why this is useful is these counselors will have direct first name contacts with staff inside all of the other organizations - they can get you on the fast track to instant help for everything from therapy to old age pensions - drug rehab - free food - crutches, emotional counseling, jobs, scholarships - I mean literally everything you might need. These people are at the central nexus of the whole social services sector and are on the inside track. They have a lot of influence and know where all of the rules can be bent and broken.

You can spend months searching around and worrying while the bills fall far behind - or you can get in and get hooked up quickly with the right help - and that can make all of the difference. Sometimes it saves lives. The fastest way to do it is to locate one of these counselors and get on their client list. They are not government people so they have a lot more flexibility in what they can and cannot do. They work twice as hard, and get paid half as much - but they are dedicated. Gov employees have to follow much more strict rules concerning the public.

You've got your public sector, and your private sector - there is also the third sector - the volunteer charity / community sector... and it is huge. Your tax dollars and charitable donations subsidized much of it - for exactly this reason - so it is time to collect on your investment.

Nothing, and I mean nothing, cuts through bureaucratic red tape faster than a phone call from one of these counselors. That exists in part because the system recognizes that it doesn't work as well as it should - and that these counselors exist kind of like the agents in the movie the Matrix - they serve a special function in the system to get things unfucked and back on the fast track - an as such enjoy a certain unofficial but nevertheless very real prestige in government departments.
